Create a token for a resource class

## Usage

`circleci runner token create <resource-class> [flags]`

## Arguments

`<resource-class>` is the runner resource class to create a token for,
in the form `namespace/name` (for example, `my-org/my-runner`) or as its ID.

## Flags

| Flag                | Description                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--jq string`       | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`            | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--nickname string` | Human-readable nickname for the token                                             |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Create a token for a resource class: 
  `circleci runner token create my-org/my-runner`
- Create a token with a nickname: 
  `circleci runner token create my-org/my-runner --nickname "prod-server-1"`
- Create a token for a resource class given by its ID: 
  `circleci runner token create 01234567-89ab-4cde-8f01-23456789abcd`
- Output as JSON (includes the token value): 
  `circleci runner token create my-org/my-runner --json`

## Details

Create a runner token for a resource class. The token value is shown only once.

CLI 0.1.x (check with `circleci version`) printed a circleci-runner-config.yaml
document. This command prints text or JSON instead. There is no replacement yet.

JSON fields: id, resource_class, resource_class_id, nickname, created_at, token
